# Lifecycle, archive, delete, and recovery

`lifecycle` is an open spine facet used by workflows and coordination. It is not a universal engine state machine: installations and kinds may use different tokens, and ordinary updates can change it subject to authorization and schema rules.

Archiving is separate. `archive_record` sets the engine-reserved `archived` facet to `true`; restoration calls the same tool with `archived:false`, which unsets the facet. Absence is the restored state—`archived=false` is not stored. Archive/restore preserves the lifecycle value and is idempotent (`changed:false` means no event was appended).

High-level `query_record` filters, `search`, `scan`, and tree browsing exclude archived records unless explicitly requested. `get_record` by exact ID can inspect archived records. `query_sql` is the lower-level escape hatch: its logical records view filters tombstones and enforces authorization but includes archived rows, whose archive state can be inspected through the reserved `facet_values.archived` entry.

`delete_record` appends a soft-delete tombstone. Tombstoned records are frozen against ordinary mutation, disappear from ordinary live traversal, and remain directly inspectable by exact ID and through history. This surface does not expose a general undelete or purge state machine; do not promise one.

Successful direct record writes return `previous_seq`: the highest event sequence on that record strictly before the write transaction began. The handle remains stable when one call emits several events; `create_record` returns `null` because no prior record stream existed. To understand a pre-write state, call `get_record` for the same record with `as_of:{"content_seq": previous_seq}`.

Compensate forward with a later update and preserve the audit trail rather than rewriting history. A field-level hand revert does not erase links, facets, or other events that landed separately, and multi-step compensation is not atomic.

Archive has its own explicit recovery path: call `archive_record` with `archived:false`. Although `delete_record` also reports its prior sequence for inspection, its tombstone is frozen and this surface exposes no compensating update or general undelete for it.
